svg.title: A toolbox release changes a line I edited myself, and the update merge request shows both: a toolbox update collides with my edit on a framework file, and I settle it in the merge request
svg.text: A toolbox release changes a line I edited myself, and the
Scenario: a toolbox update collides with my edit on a framework file, and I settle it in the merge request
My edit and the release touch the same line
The merge request shows the clash, and the developer settles it

g.text: Given the developer swapped the toolbox's CI image for their own hardened tag on the main
branch
The project came from toolbox release 1.0.0, whose .gitlab-ci.yml runs every pipeline in the toolbox image tagged 1.0.0.
The developer swapped that tag for their own build, 1.0.0-hardened, and pushed the commit to the main branch.
GitLab's page for that commit, "ci: pin our hardened image": the red line is the tag the release wrote, the green line
is the developer's.

text.tspan: sed -i 's/:1.0.0$/:1.0.0-hardened/' .gitlab-ci.yml && git commit -qam "ci: pin our hardened image" && git push -q

g.text: When the developer runs the toolbox update and it warns that the release changes the same
line
Release 1.0.1 is out, and it moves the same image line to the tag 1.0.1. The developer asks for it with one command,
from the main branch.
Copier applies the release, then a warning names .gitlab-ci.yml: "this release changed lines you had edited too". The
update still pushes the branch update-framework-devsecops and opens merge request !1 into the main branch.
Then GitLab now holds an update merge request showing both image lines as a conflict
The Changes tab of merge request !1. The answers file moves from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1, and .gitlab-ci.yml keeps both image
lines between conflict markers: the developer's 1.0.0-hardened under "<<<<<<< before updating", the release's 1.0.1
above ">>>>>>> after updating".
Nothing was dropped, and the main branch did not move.
And once the developer fixes that line on the update branch, the merge request carries their
hardened tag on the new release
On the update branch, the developer replaces the whole conflict with one line, their hardening on the new release
(1.0.1-hardened), then commits and pushes it.
The same tab now shows one plain change, from 1.0.0-hardened to 1.0.1-hardened, with no marker left. Commits counts 2,
the update and the fix, ready for review.

text.tspan: -qam "ci: keep our hardened image on 1.0.1" && git push -q

● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
